newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian 1996 budget revenue falls short.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian 1996 budget revenue falls short.

text.p: Lithuania's 1996 budget revenue collection fell short by some 356.53 million litas from the planned 6.99 billion litas, the head of the parliament budget committee said on Thursday.
Elvira Kunaviciene said that state internal debt was 1.5 billion litas during 1996 and urged improved tax collection in 1997.
The new right-wing government has set a budget for 1997 with a deficit of 697 million litas, some 100 million litas higher than the deficit set by the previous government.
She said the internal debt was composed of loans of 765 million litas, the 356 million litas that went uncollected and 776 million litas paid in subsidies to the energy sector.
Tax collection has been one of the main areas that Western advisors have urged Lithuania to improve.
In 1997, VAT is one of the main sources of revenue at a planned 3.4 billion litas.
